idea: Build-to-rent scheme underwriting support for small funds
pain: Underwriting BTR needs design, cost and operational assumptions together
verdict: Real fit and decent fees; BTR volumes and her lack of operational track record are the constraints.

why.distribution: BTR investors are adjacent to her network rather than in it.
why.demand: Underwriting support is commissioned in this market.
why.fmf: Design and cost literacy plus financial modelling; she lacks BTR operational experience.
why.defensibility: Specialist BTR consultancies compete with track records she lacks.
why.leverage: Bespoke per scheme with a reusable model.
why.tailwind: BTR is a genuine multi-year institutional allocation trend.
why.ceiling: £11k x 18 schemes = £198k, but BTR scheme volume for a solo advisor is far lower.

ceiling_arithmetic: £11k x 18 schemes = £198k. UK BTR scheme volume reaching a solo advisor is realistically 4-6 a year = £44-66k.
carries: Strong sector tailwind and a genuine need for combined design-cost-finance judgement.
kills: Deal volume. There are simply not enough schemes reaching a solo advisor to build a year on.
test: Ask two BTR investors what they outsource in underwriting.
test_pass: They name a gap she fills.
